claim_scope: First host-CLI exact-image build and platform-validation startup attempts. Runtime security PASS was not reached.

retained_attempts.note: Three exact-base copy-only images built successfully. PostgreSQL did not become healthy. The first orchestrator revision removed the failed container before retaining its logs; that diagnostic-loss defect was corrected before retry.

The host CLI verified and reused the exact built image IDs, resumed the matching retained volume, and captured the decisive log: mkdir: can't create directory '/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata': Permission denied.

root_cause.summary: The source-gated PostgreSQL base defaults to root and its image directory does not seed the new named volume with UID/GID 70 ownership. Compose correctly forces 70:70, so the entrypoint cannot create PGDATA in the root-owned volume.

decision.next_action: Preserve the v1 topology contract and failed volume evidence, then version a copy-only derived database image that establishes UID/GID 70 ownership without RUN, root runtime, secrets, network, or a Docker socket. Replay the topology contract, implementation, mutation, and real startup gates before accepting runtime PASS.
prohibited_shortcuts: Do not run PostgreSQL as root.
Do not use a privileged ownership-fix container.
Do not chown the volume through a Docker-socket-bearing workload.
Do not delete or rewrite the failed attempt before evidence retention.
